name: SQLite
subtitle: Embedded, file-based SQL database
creator: D. Richard Hipp
description: A complete SQL database in a small C library that reads and writes a single file, with no server process. It is the most widely deployed database engine in the world, and tools like Litestream, Turso and D1, plus Rails 8 defaults, make it practical for web production.

languages.youWrite: SQL through bindings in almost every language

concepts.explanation: The whole database is one file.
Flexible typing unless you use STRICT tables.
Better concurrency for readers and a writer.
Litestream and LiteFS copy it elsewhere.

codeSamples.label: Python
codeSamples.code:
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("app.db")
con.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;")
con.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT NOT NULL)")
con.execute("INSERT INTO notes (body) VALUES (?)", ("Hello SQLite",))
con.commit()
for row in con.execute("SELECT id, body FROM notes ORDER BY id DESC"):
    print(row)

cons: Only one writer at a time
Loose typing unless you opt into STRICT

pricing.summary: Free (public domain). Hosted variants such as Turso and Cloudflare D1 have their own plans.
